purpose: Session lifecycle of the engine's global state: what a load puts back, what survives an unload and why that is harmless. T14 extends it with the causal save/restore policy of every component.
method: A clean process has every engine global at its static initial value and a second load in the same process does not. The step probe (tests/step/step_probe.cpp) loads the same image again in one process and compares it with a clean one: per-unit state digest (P6_RELOAD, P6_DIGEST_PARTS) and the writable data segment right after the reset head (P6_DATA_DUMP, diffed against nm). Heap growth is measured with Apple's leaks tool on p6_cycles_probe. Every entry that changes the engine has a test that failed before the change.

status_values.reset: put back to its clean-process value at load or reset; the test named in evidence compares a reload with a clean process
status_values.rebuilt: derived again from other state before anything reads it; a reload's video and machine digests match a clean process from unit 1
status_values.noncausal: a pointer, a counter that is only written, or a feature the A500 profile never reaches
status_values.open: differs from a clean process and is not understood yet; limitation of the profile until closed

entries.at_load: bridge/lifecycle.cpp clears regs before init_m68k; m68k_reset2 sets only pc, sp and sr, so D0-D7/A0-A6 would carry the previous session
bridge/lifecycle.cpp sets vpos to 0; custom_reset never resets it, so the first unit's length depended on how long the previous session ran (905 colour clocks in the measured case)
patch 0068 puts the head on track 0 in DISK_init; a p6_reset keeps it where it was, like a real drive
patch 0069 clears them in inputdevice_reset; POTGOR read $5500 instead of $0000 in the first frame of a reload
patch 0070 clears them in clear_events; event2idx decides where MISC_handler starts its round, so the order of two events due at the same instant
patch 0071 clears it in CIA_reset; it is compared with regs.ipl_evt when an interrupt is recognised and the cycle counter restarts at every reset

p6_input_reset_keys (patch 0066) runs at every p6_reset and, from bridge/lifecycle.cpp, at every load: a reset chord held when a session ended made the first key event of the next load reset the machine

matchdevices allocates a name and a configuration name per device on every load; copy_prefs memcpy'd the pointers away. Patch 0072 gives each preference set its own strings and bridge/config.cpp frees both sets when the session ends: 2.3 KiB per cycle, 68 KB in 30 cycles, now 0 leaks
see reports/tasks/T12c.md: the registered blobs, the drive contents, the event queue and the sequence number are forgotten at unload

bridge/lifecycle.cpp sets the engine's cycle counter to 0 before p6_rtc_init and installs counter_restarts in p6_counter_restart_hook (patch 0073), which the reset head calls just before the counter starts over for EVERY kind of reset (p6_reset, the Ctrl-Amiga-Amiga chord, the reset warning): it adds the part of the unit that ran before the restart to the caller's ticks and rebases the clock, which keeps time through a reset. Before this, any guest that read the clock after a p6_reset or a reload faulted the image (p6_run_frame failed: 11), a Kickstart reads it at boot, and a first version that rebased only for p6_reset left the keyboard chord faulting
release_engine undoes exactly the stages the load reached: clock, video presentation, blob store, media identity
not cleared: per-line and per-frame drawing state that the drawing code overwrites before it reads it
not cleared: nothing reads them outside debugging (vsync_cycles is never read)
not cleared: the token of the next stream only has to be unique, p6_blob_clear closes every stream
allocated again at every load; their values are addresses of this process
not cleared: the Ricoh clock, the joystick port configuration, text pasting and the mouse time base are not reached by the A500 profile or do not show in a reload

cia_cycle_accurate is worked out once per frame (end of CIA_vsync_prehandler), so a process that has not finished a frame has it false and runs its first frame with CIA interrupts that do not wait for the E clock. A reload kept the last session's true: the keyboard interrupts of unit 1 came 8 to 11 colour clocks later and the last one stacked another PC, one byte of the stack ($F80118 instead of $F80116), for input_all and input_rotate. Patch 0074 puts it back from bridge/lifecycle.cpp at every load; a p6_reset keeps it, as a reset in a running process does
